correctness.rationale: A bivector in a four-space is decomposable iff its Plücker quadratic form is zero. The anisotropic two-plane kernel is nondegenerate, and its four-dimensional orthogonal quotient is minus type. Its norm-plane fibers have one point over zero and q+1 points over any nonzero scalar. Every nonzero decomposable bivector has q(q²-1) ordered wedge decompositions; the zero bivector has q⁵+q⁴-q. The minus-type quadric has exactly q³-q²+q zeros. The resulting exhaustive partition, explicit non-square model, and class-two group cocycle establish every formula. Actual verification exhausts q=3,5 and checks contractions for 7,11; finite checks are not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: The full commutator-word pushforward is a natural arithmetic invariant of a well-studied minimal-centralizer family. Its exact targetwise two-valued nonzero distribution, elliptic-null-cone multiplicities and surjectivity are strictly finer than aggregate commuting probabilities or contraction ranks. The result applies to every admissible alternating quotient over every odd finite field rather than a cherry-picked finite instance.
